text: Inheritance lets a new class build on an existing one, reusing its code instead of repeating it.
Animal is our base class, with a name and a generic speak method.
Dog and Cat inherit from Animal by naming it in parentheses — they get its init and attributes for free.
[chuckle] But each subclass overrides speak with its own version, so a dog barks and a cat meows.
Notice neither Dog nor Cat rewrites init — they simply inherit it from Animal.
[sniff] So creating a Dog still sets the name, using the parent's constructor automatically.
Each object then speaks in its own way, while sharing the common structure.
[sigh] The relationship is is-a — a Dog is an Animal, which isinstance confirms as true.
[groan] Inheritance shines when several classes share behavior — write it once in the parent, specialize only what differs.
